title: A Trail for the Landfall
premise: Edmund Joubert, a railroad engineer who has spent years mapping abandoned lines to stay off the books, is hired by a secretive financier to survey a coastal route where the morning tide has exposed a sea cave tied to a vanished 1890s expedition. Inside, Edmund and a ragtag crew—a disgraced cartographer, a runaway telegraph operator, and a widowed ferry captain—find evidence that the earlier party discovered something worth killing for: a vein of ore and the ledger proving a railroad baron buried his own men to claim it. As the financier's hired guns close in and the cave begins to flood with the season's storms, Edmund must choose between selling the truth or giving it away. The expedition makes it home alive only because they scatter the evidence to every town along the line at once—too public to suppress—and Edmund, once invisible, finally claims a name, a family, and a place on the map.
about_author: Jude Crane is the pen name of a former surveyor's assistant who spent six seasons in coastal British Columbia before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who know exactly how far from help they are.

chapters.title: The Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Edmund Joubert, POV. Edmund walks an abandoned spur at dawn, cataloguing decay, establishing his philosophy: the wilderness forgives nothing and forgets less. A telegram arrives offering triple pay for a coastal survey he never advertised for. Beat: wary curiosity—the trap hasn't sprung yet, but he feels its shape.

chapters.title: A Client Without a Face
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. In a port hotel, he meets Mr. Aldous Vane's lawyer instead of Vane himself: papers, money, and a condition—no names in the field notes. Edmund takes the job despite the smell of it, needing the money to buy back his father's seized homestead. Beat: compromise; he signs away a little of himself.

chapters.title: Crew of the Unwanted
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. He assembles a crew no one else will hire: Ida Marsh, a cartographer struck off the rolls for falsifying nothing but telling the truth; Pip Okonkwo, a teenage telegraph runner fleeing an apprenticeship; Captain Ruth Ellery and her ferry, the Kestrel. Beat: found family begins forming around shared exile.

chapters.title: North Along the Drowned Coast
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV. The Kestrel works up the coast through fog and derelict trestles Edmund maps from the rail. Pip proves invaluable reading old signal wires; Ida and Edmund argue over projection methods and like each other better for it. Beat: competence and camaraderie on open water.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gave Back
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. At low spring tide, the sea withdraws past any charted mark, revealing the mouth of a cave the locals call the Landfall—legend says it charges admission in lives. Ruth refuses to enter; Edmund goes in anyway with lantern and line. Beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The First Expedition
chapters.summary: Ida, POV. Inside, they find the 1890s survey camp preserved in salt air: instruments, a journal, and seven graves marked with railroad spikes. The journal belongs to Silas Crane, chief engineer, and it stops mid-sentence. Beat: grief for strangers; the past becomes present tense.

chapters.title: Crane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Pip, POV. Pip deciphers Silas Crane's coded ledger: a rich ore seam, and proof that baron Augustus Vane—grandfather to their employer—ordered the tunnel sealed with his own crew inside to hide both the deaths and the claim. Beat: horror; the money paying them is blood money twice over.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Water
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV. A second boat appears on the horizon—Vane's men, ahead of schedule. Ruth runs the Kestrel through unmarked shoals she alone knows, buying a day. Someone aboard realizes the crew was never meant to come back. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Admission Charged
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Returning to the cave for the ledger copies, Edmund triggers a collapse that traps him behind the tide line. He survives by following Silas Crane's carved escape marks—proof the first expedition almost made it out too. Beat: humility; the wilderness forgives nothing, and he nearly pays.

chapters.title: The Confession in Salt
chapters.summary: Ida, POV. Rescued at the last minute, Edmund finds a final page of Crane's journal hidden in the escape passage: not a report, but a letter to his daughter asking her to remember the men honestly. Ida recognizes the daughter's married name—her own grandmother. Beat: identity revealed; Ida has been walking toward this cave her whole life.

chapters.title: Three Versions of the Truth
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. The crew argues: sell the ledger to Vane and live rich, give it to newspapers and be ruined by lawyers, or bury it and survive unknown. Each argues from their wound—Ida for justice, Ruth for peace, Pip for being believed at all. Beat: fracture; found family tested by stakes.

chapters.title: Vane Comes North
chapters.summary: Pip, POV. Aldous Vane arrives in person aboard a private steamer, charming and terrible, offering Edmund his father's homestead free and clear—for the ledger and silence about the graves. He mentions Pip's real name and hometown, showing they were all chosen for leverage. Beat: corruption made personal.

chapters.title: The Homestead Papers
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Alone with the deed to everything he wanted, Edmund reads Silas Crane's letter again and understands what his father would have done. He burns nothing and signs nothing, and tells Vane the ledger is already gone. It isn't—yet. Beat: the first fully selfless choice; bluff as commitment.

chapters.title: Cut Wires
chapters.summary: Pip, POV. Vane's men cut the Kestrel loose and seize the harbor telegraph office, trapping the crew between storm season and gunfire. Pip rigs the old signal line Edmund mapped in chapter four—an abandoned wire nobody knows still carries current. Beat: every skill planted early now matters.

chapters.title: The Storm Season Opens
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV. The first true gale hits; the cave will flood within days, destroying or preserving the evidence depending on what they do. Ruth, who lost her husband to a sea she respected too late, chooses to run the Kestrel back into the worst water on the coast. Beat: courage as acceptance, not defiance.

chapters.title: Broadcast to Every Town
chapters.summary: Ida, POV. The plan crystallizes: copy the ledger and Crane's letter, and transmit summaries down every working telegraph line at once—twenty stations, twenty towns, too many witnesses to bury. Ida drafts the message naming all seven dead men. Beat: purpose; grief converted into testimony.

chapters.title: The Kestrel Runs
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV. Under fire from Vane's steamer, Ruth threads the drowned coast at night while Pip taps the message station to station. The Kestrel takes damage; the message gets through to eleven towns before the line dies. Beat: climax of action—cost paid in wood and blood, not lives.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Cornered at the cave mouth as the tide rises, Edmund confronts Vane among Silas Crane's graves and offers him the one thing money can't buy back: witnesses. Vane's own men, hearing the transmission confirmed, refuse to seal another tunnel. Beat: moral climax; power fails when its servants stop believing in it.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Pip, POV. The cave floods, taking the original journal and the ore seam's location back into the dark—only the testimony survives. Vane retreats to fight lawyers instead of people. Pip, who expected to be disbelieved, watches a newspaper boy shout the seven names. Beat: release; truth outlives evidence.

chapters.title: Inquiries
chapters.summary: Ida, POV. Weeks later, hearings begin. Ida testifies under her full name, restoring her grandmother's story and her own standing. Vane's empire cracks publicly; Edmund's father's homestead is returned by court order, unsought. Beat: vindication without triumphalism.

chapters.title: The Map We Keep
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Edmund and Ida redraw the coastal charts together, marking the closed lines and leaving the Landfall deliberately unmapped—some admissions should stay charged. Ruth refits the Kestrel; Pip apprentices properly, on their own terms. Beat: quiet joy; family chosen and kept.

chapters.title: A Trail for the Landfall
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. A year on, the crew surveys an honest contract together, and at spring tide they return to stand above the flooded cave and read the seven names aloud. Edmund, once invisible, signs the new chart with his full name beside four others. Beat: resolution—identity, power rightly held, and home found in people, not places.
